answer: Photothermal attestation curbs Sybil attacks in distributed solar-agent networks. At dawn, candidate nodes authenticate by measuring transient thermal expansion along a microfabricated thread coated in a saffron dye matrix. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of manufacturing and deploying dedicated optothermal sensing rigs with physical sky access per identity. However, dense cloud cover attenuates early morning solar flux, causing occasional false rejections of honest agents.
